sections.title: Paywall Footer — every setting
sections.summary: The bottom of the paywall — the purchase (subscribe) button and its label and box styling, the auto-renew disclosure note, the footer background and element order, and the restore / terms-of-use / privacy-policy legal links with their URLs and styling. This guide documents every setting of the Paywall Footer block, grouped by area. Each setting matches a real control in the screen editor.

sections.title: Paywall Footer section
sections.summary: The Paywall Footer is the bottom action zone of a paywall and holds your single most important conversion control: the purchase/subscribe button, plus the auto-renew disclosure and legal links (Restore, Terms of Use, Privacy Policy). For an ad-ready paywall you must have a working purchase button and filled-in Terms and Privacy links, because ad networks and app stores reject paywalls without them. It only appears on paywall screens.

sections.title: Where it appears
sections.summary: Covered screen types: Paywall.

sections.title: Auto-renew text spacing
sections.summary: Adds padding around the auto-renew disclosure text on each side — top, bottom, left, and right (left/right flip for right-to-left languages). The defaults are fine for most paywalls; this is optional fine-tuning. Add a little top spacing if you want to separate the disclosure from the button above it.

sections.title: Auto-renew disclosure styling
sections.summary: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the auto-renew disclosure text. Keep it small and quiet relative to your main button — but it must stay clearly readable. App Store and ad-network rules require the renewal terms be legible, so avoid tiny sizes or low-contrast colors that effectively hide the disclosure.

sections.title: Configure auto-renew disclosure text
sections.summary: Sets the text displayed below the purchase button to explain subscription renewal terms (default: Auto-renews monthly. Cancel anytime.). Supports template variables like duration, price, and custom links.

sections.title: Color the footer background
sections.summary: Sets the fill color of the whole footer block, which holds the purchase button, the auto-renew note, and the legal links (default a dark tone). Pick a color that makes your button pop and keeps the renewal note and legal links readable. If you switch to a light footer, darken those text colors so everything stays legible.

sections.title: Order the button and renewal note
sections.summary: Sets whether the purchase button sits above the auto-renew disclosure or below it. Button-first is the common, conversion-friendly default. Put the disclosure first when you want the renewal terms visible right above the button so users read them before tapping — often the safer choice for compliance.

sections.title: Legal links row spacing
sections.summary: Adds padding around the whole row of legal links — Restore, Terms, and Privacy together — on each side: top, bottom, left, and right (left/right flip for right-to-left languages). The defaults are fine; this is optional fine-tuning. Add a little top and bottom spacing so the links sit clearly below the disclosure without crowding.

sections.title: Privacy link styling
sections.summary: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the Privacy Policy link. Match it to the Restore and Terms links so the legal row looks unified. Small and muted is fine, but it must stay readable — required legal links hidden in unreadable text can get your paywall rejected.

sections.title: Configure privacy policy link
sections.summary: Sets the text for the privacy policy link (default: Privacy Policy). This link appears in the legal links section and navigates to your privacy document when tapped.

sections.title: Link your Privacy Policy page
sections.summary: The full https:// web address your Privacy Policy link opens when tapped. Fill this in for any paid funnel — a live Privacy Policy is required by app stores and ad platforms once you collect payment or data. Leaving it empty disables the link and leaves the paywall non-compliant, so don't publish an ad-ready paywall with this blank.

sections.title: Style the purchase button box
sections.summary: Controls the look of the purchase button itself — fill color, border, corner radius, size, full-width toggle, padding, gradient, shadow, animation, and icon (the label text is styled separately). For ad funnels, a full-width button with a high-contrast accent fill and rounded corners is the proven setup. Make this the boldest element on the screen so the path to purchase is unmistakable.

sections.title: Recover users who cancel checkout
sections.summary: Lets you send people who start checkout but back out to a cheaper plan or discount offer instead of just closing the dialog. Catching abandoners this way can recover lost revenue, but you must build that follow-up screen first and connect it here. Leave it empty until you have one — then the dialog simply closes and the user stays on the paywall.

sections.title: Set space inside the button
sections.summary: Sets the padding between the button's label and its edges — top, bottom, left, and right (left/right swap automatically for right-to-left languages). Use generous top and bottom padding so the button feels large and tappable. A cramped call-to-action looks less clickable and lowers taps on mobile.

sections.title: Style the purchase button label
sections.summary: Controls the look of the text inside the purchase button — font, size, weight, color, alignment, and spacing — not the button box itself, which you style under 'Style purchase button box and appearance'. This is your main call-to-action, so make the label large, bold, and high-contrast against the button fill. Weak or hard-to-read button text directly costs you taps and sales.

sections.title: Configure purchase button text
sections.summary: Sets the visible label on the purchase subscribe button (default: Subscribe Now). The text supports template variables like pricing, duration, and custom countdown labels for dynamic personalization.

sections.title: Restore link styling
sections.summary: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the footer 'Restore Purchases' link. Style it to match the Terms and Privacy links beside it so the legal row reads as one consistent group — small and muted, but still legible. Don't make it look like your main button.

sections.title: Configure restore purchases link
sections.summary: Sets the text for the restore purchases link (default: Restore Purchases). This link appears in the legal links section below the auto-renew label and allows users to restore prior subscriptions on iOS.

sections.title: Terms link styling
sections.summary: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the Terms of Use link. Keep it consistent with the Restore and Privacy links beside it — small and muted is fine, but it must stay readable. Burying required legal links in unreadable micro-text invites store rejection and ad-network flags.

sections.title: Configure terms of use link
sections.summary: Sets the text for the terms of use link (default: Terms of Use). This link appears in the legal links section and navigates to your terms document when tapped.

sections.title: Link your Terms of Use page
sections.summary: The full https:// web address your Terms of Use link opens when tapped. Fill this in for any paid funnel — a live Terms link is effectively required by app stores and ad networks. Leaving it empty disables the link and leaves your paywall non-compliant, so never ship an ad-ready paywall with this blank.

sections.title: • Background opacity
sections.summary: How see-through the text background fill is, from 0% (invisible) to 100% (solid). Only matters when a background color is set.

sections.title: • Background radius
sections.summary: Corner rounding (px) of the text background fill; higher is softer.

sections.title: • Font family
sections.summary: The typeface of the auto-renew note.

sections.title: • Font size
sections.summary: Text size of the auto-renew note in pixels.

sections.title: • Font weight
sections.summary: How bold the text is, from Thin through Bold to Black.

sections.title: • Line height
sections.summary: Vertical spacing between lines of text — raise it to give multi-line text more breathing room.

sections.title: • Strikethrough color
sections.summary: Color of a line-through decoration when the text is struck out (for example, an old price).

sections.title: • Text align
sections.summary: Horizontal alignment of the text: start (left), center, or end (right).

sections.title: • Text background color
sections.summary: An optional fill drawn behind the auto-renew note text (a highlight pill). Off unless you set it; leave empty for plain text on the screen background.

sections.title: • Text color
sections.summary: The color of the auto-renew note text. Keep enough contrast with the background that it stays readable.

translations.en: Sets the font, size, weight, color, and alignment of the auto-renew disclosure text. Keep it small and quiet relative to your main button — but it must stay clearly readable. App Store and ad-network rules require the renewal terms be legible, so avoid tiny sizes or low-contrast colors that effectively hide the disclosure.

nodes.label: Auto-renew note & footer layout · Order the button and renewal note

translations.en: Order the button and renewal note

Sets whether the purchase button sits above the auto-renew disclosure or below it. Button-first is the common, conversion-friendly default. Put the disclosure first when you want the renewal terms visible right above the button so users read them before tapping — often the safer choice for compliance.

nodes.label: Auto-renew note & footer layout · Color the footer background

translations.en: Sets the fill color of the whole footer block, which holds the purchase button, the auto-renew note, and the legal links (default a dark tone). Pick a color that makes your button pop and keeps the renewal note and legal links readable. If you switch to a light footer, darken those text colors so everything stays legible.
